title.value: Learning active tactile perception through belief-space control
title.justification: The title clearly states the focus on learning active tactile perception, which aligns with the content of the paper described in the abstract and introduction.
title.quote: Learning active tactile perception through belief-space control

extractions.description: This paper proposes a framework for robots to autonomously learn tactile exploration policies using belief-space control to estimate object physical properties such as mass and height. The method involves a generative world model and information-gathering model predictive controller, validated in simulation and real-robot experiments.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The primary focus of the paper is on robotics and the development of tactile perception policies for robots. While this could indirectly influence sustainable practices, it does not directly address climate or ecological sustainable development.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: The primary focus of the paper is on active tactile perception for robots to learn and extract object properties autonomously.

primary_category.justification: The paper does not directly address any specific area of Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development. It focuses on robotic technology development without a clear link to sustainable practices.
primary_category.quote: Robots operating in an open world will encounter novel objects with unknown physical properties, such as mass, friction, or size. These robots will need to sense these properties through interaction prior to performing downstream tasks with the objects.

secondary_categories.justification: The content does not cover any secondary climate or ecological sustainable development aspects.
secondary_categories.quote: The focus is on developing generative models for robotic perception and control.

primary_sub_category.quote: We propose a method that autonomously learns tactile exploration policies by developing a generative world model.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The paper does not engage with any sub-categories relevant to Climate or Ecological Sustainable Development.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: The method involves learning a model that can infer the dynamical properties from a sequence of force and proprioceptive measurements.

applications.justification: The paper discusses applications in robotics, specifically autonomous tactile exploration for understanding object properties.
applications.quote: We evaluate our method on three simulated tasks where the goal is to estimate a desired object property (mass, height or toppling height) through physical interaction.
